tasks.short: Search journals for new literature, read it, talk with colleagues, and take part in professional conferences.

steps.what: Lecturer searches journals and tables of contents for current literature
Lecturer reads current literature in the field
Lecturer talks with colleagues about developments
Lecturer participates in professional conferences

tasks.design: Saved searches and table-of-contents alerts in the library's discovery and citation databases ({OTHER}) send new titles in the lecturer's topics each week, so journals are not searched one by one. Reading, talking with colleagues and conferences stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Journals were checked one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Citation databases send saved-search and table-of-contents alerts.
tasks.still_hard: Books and conference talks are not in the alerts.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing at a conference which new idea colleagues take seriously.
tasks.altitude: Less searching of journals; reading stays.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: from field developments to the conference attended; own research is outside.
Input contract: library licences the databases; fallback is checking journals.
Reading and conferences do not change.

incremental.description: Lecturer tunes saved searches as topics shift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: alerts miss several journals in the field, so s1 keeps 80 (3.5); high: alerts cover the field as assumed (9.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile exam questions, check the final exam, administer it, grade short answers and essay questions, and compute final grades.

steps.what: Lecturer compiles examination questions in a document
Lecturer checks the final exam paper: questions fit the course outcomes, the answer key is right and the wording is clear
Lecturer administers the examination in the hall
Exam office scans the answer sheets into the exam tool
Lecturer grades short-answer examinations: one by one today, group by group of scanned answers after the change

loop.input: Scanned short answers per question and the answer model.
loop.output: Groups of similar answers per question.
loop.check: The lecturer grades each group and confirms every grade per student; a sample of grouped answers is double-marked by hand each exam.
loop.stop: One grouping per question; answers the model cannot place go to the lecturer one by one.
loop.why_not_simpler: Students phrase the same point differently; string matching does not group them.

steps.what: Lecturer grades essay questions
Lecturer enters marks in a spreadsheet and computes final grades

tasks.design: Questions are kept in an item bank in the exam tool ({LMS}) with item statistics from earlier use, so exams are compiled from tested items instead of written from scratch. Short answers are scanned and grouped by similarity, so the lecturer grades each group once and confirms every grade; a sample is double-marked. Essays are graded by the lecturer as now. The tool totals marks and computes grades instead of a spreadsheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exams were written from scratch and each answer graded and totalled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Exam tools hold item banks and group similar answers.
tasks.still_hard: Literature exams are mostly essays, which do not group.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a strong reading that the answer model did not foresee.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer grades groups and essays instead of totalling marks.

evidence.claim: Gradescope groups similar answers so each group is graded once.
At Penn State Harrisburg, answer grouping 'reduces grading time by over half' on 170 physics exams; one professor's estimate in a vendor story.
AI used to evaluate learning outcomes is high-risk; duties apply from 2 December 2027.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: from the exam due to final grades; appeals are outside.
Input contract: answer sheets scannable; fallback is grading one by one.
A DPIA and the examination board's consent come before use.
Scanning the answer sheets is exam office work, shown in s3b. s1 keeps 50 for new items; s4 keeps 50 because every answer is still seen and every grade confirmed; s6 keeps 20 for checking totals.
research_questions: How often does double-marking change a grouped grade?

already_counted.description: Lecturer confirms grades per answer group.

incremental.description: Lecturer double-marks a sample of grouped answers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many answers do not group well, so s4 keeps 85, and the item bank is thin, so s1 keeps 80 (14.7); high: grouping and item bank as assumed (29.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise and assist students in office hours, arrange appointments, and send follow-up links and materials.

steps.what: Lecturer advises and assists students in office hours
Student books an office-hour slot on the booking page
Lecturer arranges office-hour appointments: by e-mail today; after the change students book and the lecturer handles only changes and clashes
Lecturer sends follow-up links and materials to students

tasks.design: Students book office-hour slots themselves in the lecturer's booking page ({CALENDAR}), so appointments are not arranged by e-mail. Common follow-up material (writing guides, reading lists) sits in a course resource page that the lecturer links to. Advising students stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appointments were arranged by e-mail back and forth.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendars offer booking pages with set slots.
tasks.still_hard: Students in crisis do not book slots.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a student who is struggling beyond the course.
tasks.altitude: Fewer e-mails about appointments; advising stays.

evidence.claim: Calendars offer booking pages with set slots.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student visit to the follow-up sent; formal study advice is outside.
Input contract: booking page published; fallback is e-mail.
Students book in less time than e-mailing; their booking is shown in s1b. s2 keeps 30 for changes; s3 keeps 60 because the lecturer still picks material and writes a short note.

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps the resource page current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the students still e-mail for appointments, so s2 keeps 65 (8.4); high: most book on the page as assumed (13.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile literature and bibliographies, read and analyse texts, write the article, format references, check the final manuscript, and submit it to the journal.

steps.what: Lecturer compiles literature and bibliographies for the research

loop.input: The research question and the library's catalogue and citation databases.
loop.check: Each title must resolve by DOI or library catalogue, else it is dropped; the lecturer reads each abstract and keeps only titles that bear on the research question.
loop.stop: One search per question; if nothing resolves, the lecturer searches by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Topics are described in many ways; keyword search misses related work.

steps.what: Lecturer conducts research by reading and analysing texts
Lecturer writes findings for professional journals or books
Lecturer formats references and the manuscript to the journal's style by hand
Lecturer checks the final manuscript: the argument, quotes and references are right
Lecturer submits the manuscript to publish findings through the journal portal

tasks.design: A research search tool over the library's citation databases ({OTHER}) suggests related titles with abstracts; any title that does not resolve by DOI or catalogue is dropped, and the lecturer chooses what to read. A reference manager stores the sources and formats citations and the bibliography in the journal's style, so references are not formatted by hand. Reading, analysing, writing and submitting stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature was searched by keyword and references formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Citation databases suggest related work; reference managers format citations.
tasks.still_hard: Older and non-English literature is poorly indexed.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a new reading of a familiar text.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer spends more time reading and writing.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and foundational papers.
Funder rules bar referees from using generative AI on proposals.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the manuscript submitted; peer review is outside.
Input contract: library licences the databases; fallback is keyword search.
The lecturer writes and submits every manuscript.
research_questions: Do suggested titles add work the lecturer would have missed?

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps the reference library tidy.

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript exactly as checked by the lecturer in s5, submitted once to the named journal through its portal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: archival research with few indexed sources, so suggestions help little and s1 keeps 90 (8.5); high: topics covered in the databases as assumed (14.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The lecturer keeps reading, advising, grading essays and writing research; journal checking, answer-by-answer grading, e-mail scheduling and reference formatting shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using item banks and answer grouping
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer with more time for research and students.
